title: Pauri 13: trusting, awareness
hookLine: mannai: by trust the mind becomes aware and knows all realms (Japji 13)
tomorrow: Pauri 14: trusting, the path is clear

lines: A CHILD ON A PARENT'S SHOULDERS.
cards: You'd think trust would make you sleepy: relax, you've got this, lean back. But watch a child on a parent's shoulders at a parade.

Because she's safe up there, she sees everything: the drummers, the balloons, the dog in the crowd. The child on the ground, gripping a hand and worried about getting lost, sees knees. Safety doesn't dull her.
It frees her attention to look around. Pauri 13 makes a claim like that: trusting doesn't put the mind to sleep. It wakes it up.

teach.b: Pauri 13 opens: mannai surat hovai man budh. By trusting, surat comes into the mind and the understanding.
Surat, today's word, carries real weight in Sikh teaching: awareness, attention, consciousness, the part of you that's awake and noticing.
In Sikh thought, surat is what attunes to the shabad, the Word, the way a radio tunes to a station.

In the Sidh Gosht, Guru Nanak's dialogue with the yogis, the Word is called the Guru and the attentive mind, surat, the disciple. The pauri goes on, in paraphrase. By trusting, one knows of all the realms, every world.

By trusting, one doesn't take blows to the face. By trusting, one doesn't go off with the messenger of death. And the refrain: such is the Name of the Stainless One, known only to the one who trusts it in the mind.
Before knowing all realms, before escaping fear, the first gift of trust is that you wake up. Listening gave direction; trusting gives attention. It fits an ordinary Tuesday, too.
When you're anxious, attention shrinks to one tight spot, the worry.
When you trust, it opens: the light on the wall, the tone in someone's voice, what the moment is actually asking.

One way to hear the blows to the face and the messenger of death is as the stanza's picture of fear; some commentators read them as what awaits after death. A mind that trusts doesn't flinch at every shadow.

how: Pauri 13 is part of the morning Japji; Sikh teachers speak of surat, awareness, being joined to the shabad as central to practice, especially while listening to kirtan or reciting the Name.

games.q: what's inside Pauri 13 — tap the pairs.
p: what the one who trusts escapes

s: in Pauri 13, trusting makes the mind dull and sleepy
the first gift it names is surat: awareness comes into the mind.
surat is a key word in Sikh teaching about the Word
surat joined to shabad, awareness tuned to the Word, is at the heart of the path.
Pauri 13 ends with the same refrain as Pauri 12
such is the Name of the Stainless One, known to the one who trusts.

games.q: you trust, fully. according to Pauri 13, what's the first thing that happens?
games.why: mannai surat hovai man budh: by trusting, awareness comes into the mind and understanding, and only then the knowing of all realms.

practice: Let attention move slowly down your body, from the top of your head to your feet, just noticing, fixing nothing. Then feel the whole body at once, one shape, breathing, and rest there.
If the mind narrows onto a worry, widen it again to the whole body.

wordCard.voice: Surat. Awareness, attention, the waking consciousness that tunes to the Word. By trusting, Pauri 13 says, surat comes.
